bearerAuth.description: A `tm_` API key, minted on a project's API keys page. It reads its organization and that project, within the scopes it was minted with: an upload needs `ingest`, as an export does, and every other lane here `read`.

info.description: The API a `tm_` token opens. Every response that is not a success is an RFC 9457 problem document, and a client switches on its `type` rather than on its prose.

get.description: Each first run of an agent, in one environment, to carry a release, a model or a prompt's version its runs there had not carried in the 30 days before, the newest first, 500 at most, `more` saying the window held more. An agent past 24 changes of one kind in a UTC day is marked no further that day, its last shown one `capped`.

get.description: The organization the key belongs to — its id, its slug, its name and its owner's address and name. The slug is what the console's URLs name it by: set from the name it was created under, when that reads as one, and moved only when the URL is changed in Settings; the id never moves. A key is minted on one project of one organization, so this answers for the caller's organization and for no other.

post.description: Up to 100 scores, as `{"scores": [...]}`, of runs, spans or sessions that already ended; a score on a span still open rides on it as OpenTelemetry's `gen_ai.evaluation.result` event instead. Each names a `run_id`, a `run_id` and a `span_id`, or a `session_id`; a `name` of 1 to 64 characters; a `data_type` of `number`, with a finite `value` and an optional `range_min` and `range_max`, `boolean`, with a `value` of 1 or 0, or `category`, with 1 to 10 `categories`; and optionally a `version` of what scored, up to 64 characters, and an `id`, a UUID of the caller's, under which a score sent again replaces itself. What it scores is not looked up, since a run's spans may land after its score. A score is metadata, kept in every content mode, and a request is metered as an export is.

requestBody.description: A JSON body, as the description gives it.

400.description: No score, more than 100, a body past 512 KiB, or one breaking a score's rules, named by its place; none is kept.
